_nota: nivel: 'principal' (main) or 'secundario' (secondary). 'atributos' = geological criteria 0-1 assigned by the team (PRELIMINARY). 'medidos' = measured data from data/datos_completos_8_sitios.xlsx (NASA POWER 2020-2026 and NASA MODIS MOD11A2 v061 via AppEEARS); null = no data. 'atributos_operativos' is written by scripts/calcular_atributos.py: do not edit by hand.

lugares.resumen: Tropical dry forest with a heavily eroded landscape of red and gray gullies.
lugares.porque: Its layers of sediments and clays exposed by erosion resemble the stratified deposits of craters such as Gale or Jezero. It is a good place to test rovers, instruments and sampling protocols.

citas.nota: Proposed as a Mars analog by Bolivar-Torres et al. (2026), for its geomorphology and climate.

lugares.resumen: Underground halite (rock salt) mine that houses the Salt Cathedral.
lugares.porque: It combines salt deposits, comparable to the chloride deposits on Mars, with an enclosed underground environment, useful for simulating lava-tube habitats and studying salt-loving microorganisms.

citas.nota: Listed as an extreme (hypersaline) environment for future astrobiology studies by Bolivar-Torres et al. (2026).

lugares.notas_datos: MODIS measures the surface of the town, not the inside of the mine; its value as an analog is the stable underground environment.

lugares.resumen: Colombia's largest desert, with dunes, dry plains and coastal salt flats (Manaure).
lugares.porque: Aridity, intense sunlight, poor soils and evaporite salt flats make it an analog of the dry plains and salt deposits of Mars.

citas.nota: Proposed as a Mars analog by Bolivar-Torres et al. (2026): gypsum substrate and wind-eroded yardangs compared with Gale Crater and Meridiani Planum. The Manaure saltern is also listed as an extreme environment.

datos.valor: Dunes, salt flats, constant wind, high radiation
Testing solar power, dust and evaporites

lugares.notas_datos: The sampling point falls over the sea, so there is no MODIS data. It still needs to be moved inland.

lugares.resumen: Semi-arid area near Ráquira with eroded, clay-rich soils.
lugares.porque: Erosion and exposed clays in a high-altitude climate.

citas.nota: Described as a potential analog location by Bolivar-Torres et al. (2026), with endolithic microbes in a semi-arid setting.

lugares.resumen: Active glacier-capped volcano in Los Nevados National Park.
lugares.porque: Ice over volcanic rock, cold, altitude and fumaroles: an ice-volcano interaction similar to the one proposed for some regions of Mars.

citas.nota: Proposed as a Mars analog by Leal et al. (2026): biogeochemistry of its periglacial slopes.

lugares.notas_datos: POWER air temperature (~50 km cell) averages the region, not the summit; cold is based on MODIS land surface temperature.

lugares.resumen: Glaciated volcano in Los Nevados National Park.
lugares.porque: Ice, cold and high-mountain volcanic soils.

citas.nota: Los Nevados National Park is cited as a Mars analog for its multiple extremophile conditions by Bolivar-Torres et al. (2026).

lugares.notas_datos: POWER air temperature (~50 km cell) averages the region, not the summit; cold is based on MODIS land surface temperature.

lugares.resumen: Pacific island known for its komatiites, very rare ultramafic lavas.
lugares.porque: Komatiites formed at very high temperatures, like ancient lavas on other planets.

citas.nota: Proposed as a terrestrial analog of Syrtis Major (Mars) by Tovar et al. (2026), based on geochemical meta-analyses and compositional figures of merit.

lugares.notas_datos: Only 25% of nighttime MODIS observations are valid because of cloud cover.

lugares.resumen: Hot springs rich in salts and sulfates.
lugares.porque: Hydrothermal systems are candidates for having hosted life on ancient Mars.

citas.nota: Described as the most studied geothermal site in Colombia's Eastern Cordillera, with thermophilic microbes, by Bolivar-Torres et al. (2026).
